advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether an unparseable/omitted container row in the docker-stats census should be surfaced (e.g. a parse-failure counter) rather than silently dropped while container_stats_ok still reads 1.
evidence: `else if (unit != "B" && unit != "") next` (observability.sh:248) drops the row for any unit not in the KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB/B set
`container_stats_ok=1` is set inside the per-row `while read` loop (observability.sh:253), so it reflects 'at least one row parsed', not 'every running container was measured'

The comment at observability.sh:261-264 justifies container_stats_ok only for the whole-census-empty case (timeout vs. nothing running); it does not cover a census that partially parsed and dropped a container silently
advisory.finding: In the container-census awk, a row whose MemUsage carries an unrecognized unit is silently dropped via `next`, yet container_stats_ok is still set to 1 by any other parseable row. A container present in `docker stats` output but with an unparseable unit therefore disappears from container_memory_rss_bytes with no lowered heartbeat to signal the omission — the per-container measurement fails open for that container.
scenarios: A docker version emits a MemUsage spelling outside the accepted binary/decimal set for one container while others parse fine
A container reports MemUsage as `--` during a restart while siblings report real values — that container is omitted with container_stats_ok=1

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the inspect.getsource grep in test_both_gate_entry_points_wrap_themselves_in_the_measurement with a behavioral test that invokes review_plan/verify_completion (internals mocked) and asserts a GATE_PEAK_RSS marker carrying the correct gate label is emitted.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py:164-166: `for func, gate in ((review_plan, "plan_review"), (verify_completion, "verify_completion")): source = inspect.getsource(func); assert f'gate_peak_rss("{gate}"' in source`

The added integration lines `with gate_peak_rss("plan_review", ticket_id):` (plan_review/__init__.py:277) and `with gate_peak_rss("verify_completion", ticket_id):` (completion.py) have no behavioral test — the other unit tests invoke `peak_rss.gate_peak_rss(...)` directly with a pass/raise body and never drive `review_plan`/`verify_completion`, so this grep is the sole guard on the actual wiring.
Litmus (Rule 4): renaming or re-expressing the wrapping call while preserving marker emission would break this assertion despite no behavior change — a change-detector, not a behavior verifier.
advisory.finding: test_both_gate_entry_points_wrap_themselves_in_the_measurement asserts on the literal source text of the functions under test (inspect.getsource(func) contains 'gate_peak_rss("..."') instead of exercising behavior. It is source-grepping / a change-detector: a behavior-preserving refactor (aliasing the import, extracting a shared wrapper, reformatting the call) breaks it with no observable-behavior change, and it verifies neither that the marker is actually emitted when review_plan/verify_completion run nor that the correct gate label reaches the marker.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drive each entry point with its internal callee (_run_completion_at_handle / the plan-review body) monkeypatched to a no-op and gate_source mocked, then assert _marker_records(capsys.readouterr().err) contains exactly one record with the expected gate value.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize the `container` dimension to a stable service identity (strip the per-deploy SHA/port suffix from the mcp container name) so per-container RSS does not create a new billed metric series on every blue-green deploy.
evidence: Ticket 9ea3 RCA: container names observed as `rebar-mcp-8db373933654-8093` then `rebar-mcp-3e04025b684e-8092` across deploys — the SHA+port churns each cutover
The `mount` precedent it cites (disk_used_percent, dimension = a stable path like /var/gerrit) has bounded, stable dimension values; a churning container name does not.
advisory.finding: The per-container gauge keys a CloudWatch `container` dimension on `docker stats {{.Name}}`, but the MCP container name embeds a per-deploy commit SHA and port (`${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}`), so every blue-green deploy emits a brand-new dimension value. That is unbounded custom-metric cardinality: each unique `container=` value is a distinct, separately-billed CloudWatch metric retained for ~15 months, and it also breaks the change's own 'which resident set grew across containers' goal because the mcp series has no continuity across deploys.
scenarios: Frequent autodeploys (this box redeploys mcp on every merge tick) each mint a new `container` dimension value, accumulating dead metric series indefinitely.
An operator graphs mcp RSS over a week and sees a fragmented series that resets on every deploy.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the awk/loop, derive a stable service label from $cname (e.g. strip a trailing `-[0-9a-f]{12}-[0-9]+` blue-green suffix, or map to the compose service name) before using it as the CloudWatch `container` dimension value.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 272 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
